gaoshou.intro.page1.title: Star: Your Second Resource
gaoshou.intro.page1.body:
Gaoshou plays differently from the other characters, so here is a quick crash course.

Unlike everyone else, many Gaoshou cards cost [color=#B03A1E]Star[/color] to play. Run out of Star and all the Energy in the world will not help — those cards simply will not come out!
gaoshou.intro.page2.title: Where Stars Come From
gaoshou.intro.page2.body:
Do not worry: plenty of Gaoshou cards hand you Star, like [color=#B03A1E]Linked Palms[/color] in your starting deck.

Star matters a lot, so keep an eye out for cards that make it!

A tip: keep the Star your deck makes roughly equal to the Star it spends.
gaoshou.intro.page3.title: Meet Your Amulet
gaoshou.intro.page3.body:
Early on, few cards make Star — that is what your starter relic, the [color=#B03A1E]Gaoshou Amulet[/color], is for.

It sits in the top-left corner; click it to read the details.

Your uses are limited, so plan your play order!
gaoshou.intro.page3.left: The number in the relic's bottom-right corner is how many uses are left this turn.
gaoshou.intro.page4.title: Do Not Burn Your Stars
gaoshou.intro.page4.body:
Star is scarce early on, so here is some strong advice: try to end each turn with 1 Star banked.

If you have to, spending health to block an attack can be worth it to save Star.

Do not let that go in one ear and out the other — this comes from experience!
gaoshou.intro.page4.left: Star does not refill on its own, but whatever is left at the end of a turn carries over.
gaoshou.firstwin.title: After Your First Fight
gaoshou.firstwin.body:
Your starting deck is wildly inconsistent, so grab [color=#B03A1E]Star generation[/color], [color=#B03A1E]card draw[/color] and [color=#B03A1E]cheap cards[/color] fast.

Good news, though: the starting deck is tiny, so building a fresh deck is surprisingly easy.

When you loot, think hard about whether the card really fits your deck!
